title: Prebiotic Blends and Remission in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Brazilian Year-Long Nonrandomized Pilot Trial
content: Background/Objectives: Long-term evidence on microbiome-targeted nutraceuticals in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is limited; we evaluated two regimens over 12 months. Methods: In this single-center, double-blind, nonrandomized, two-arm pilot trial, patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) or Crohn’s disease (CD) on stable standard-of-care therapy received fructooligosaccharides, galactooligosaccharides, yeast β-glucan, and minerals, alone (Suppl) or with silymarin (Suppl Plus), and were assessed at baseline, 6, and 12 months. The primary outcome was remission or mild activity at 12 months (UC, Mayo endoscopic subscore; CD, Simple Endoscopic Score for Crohn’s Disease). Secondary outcomes included fecal calprotectin, C-reactive protein (CRP), 16S rRNA gene profiles, and fecal nuclear magnetic resonance metabolomics. Registration: Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials, RBR-7hvd26h. Results: Of 87 participants enrolled, 75 completed follow-up (UC, n=50; CD, n=25); four died. In UC, remission or mild activity increased from 44.0% to 82.0% (p<0.001), and median calprotectin declined from 406 to 286 µg/g (p=0.046); CRP was unchanged. In CD, it remained 88.0% (p=1.000), without calprotectin change (p=0.968). Remission did not differ between arms (UC, p=1.000; CD, p=0.593). Among completers, gastrointestinal adverse effects were self-limited; flatulence increased from 2.7% to 16.0% (p=0.009). Genus-level α-diversity increased, and Dorea and Blautia were enriched in UC at 6 months; community structure did not differ between arms. In UC, fecal xanthine (+139%), 4-pyridoxate (+130%), and nicotinate (+105%) increased. Conclusions: In this nonrandomized, single-center pilot without placebo, 12-month supplementation was associated with increased remission and reduced fecal calprotectin in UC; silymarin conferred no significant advantage. Randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter trials are warranted.
